title: envelope
description: The outer shape every answer of every app shares: what it is, where it came from, the data and the errors. One shape lets any reader (a person, a script, an AI agent, control-room) read every app's answers the same way, from the CLI or over HTTP (ADR-S02, ADR-S03). Version 2 names where an answer comes from source instead of ran, and gives each error as a Problem (problem/v1, ADR-S21). version/v1, the version answer, stays on envelope/v1 for good.

apiVersion.description: The form the answer is in, as <org>/<app>/<family>/v<n>. Everything an app answers carries a version, so a reader knows which schema to read it by before reading anything else (ADR-S15).

kind.description: The kind of answer, such as BlockList or Version. With apiVersion it names the schema the data meets, so a reader never guesses the data's shape (ADR-S15).

source.description: Where the answer comes from (ADR-S08), so a reader that gathers answers from many things, apps and versions can tell each answer's source apart.

name.description: The thing the answer is about (a board, a design, a project). One server serving many things names each answer with its own thing, so a reader that gathers answers from many things (a read over a pattern or a connection, control-room) can tell them apart.

app.description: The product ID of the app that answered; a reader such as servers uses it to tell its own app on a port.

version.description: The version of the app that answered; a reader such as servers uses it to tell its own app on a port.

contract.description: The contract version the answer is in.

data.description: The answer itself; its shape is the kind's schema. The envelope leaves it open, so every kind shares one envelope and adds only its own data.

errors.description: What went wrong, one Problem per error (problem/v1, ADR-S21); empty when the answer is good. It is always there, so a reader checks one list on every answer and decides by each Problem's type and reason (ADR-S03).
